title: Statistics - Calculating and Comparing Measures of Central Tendency and Spread
topic: Statistics - Mean, Median, Mode, Range, IQR
subject: Mathematics

questions.question: The scores of 7 students in a test are: 12, 15, 18, 15, 20, 15, 22. What is the mode?
questions.explanation: The mode is the value that appears most frequently. 15 appears 3 times, more than any other score.

questions.question: The heights of 5 plants (in cm) are: 10, 12, 14, 16, 18. What is the median height?
questions.explanation: The data is already in order. With 5 values (odd), the median is the middle (3rd) value: 14 cm.

questions.question: The scores of 6 students are: 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18. What is the mean score?
questions.explanation: Mean = Sum of values ÷ Number of values = (8+10+12+14+16+18) ÷ 6 = 78 ÷ 6 = 13.

questions.question: A data set has values: 5, 8, 12, 15, 20. What is the range?
The ages of 8 children are: 5, 6, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12. What is the lower quartile (Q1)?
questions.explanation: With n=8, Q1 is at position (n+1)/4 = 2.25. Interpolate between 2nd value (6) and 3rd value (6): Q1 = 6.

questions.question: A data set has lower quartile Q1 = 25 and upper quartile Q3 = 45. What is the interquartile range (IQR)?
The weights (kg) of 7 boxes: 10, 12, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20. What is the upper quartile (Q3)?
questions.explanation: With n=7, Q3 is at position 3(n+1)/4 = 6th value. Ordered data: 10, 12, 12, 14, 16, [18], 20. Q3 = 18.

questions.question: The number of books read by 9 students: 2, 3, 3, 4, 5, 5, 5, 6, 7. What is the median?
questions.explanation: With n=9 (odd), the median is the 5th value in ordered data: 2, 3, 3, 4, [5], 5, 5, 6, 7. Median = 5.

questions.question: A frequency table shows: Score 1-5: 2 students, 6-10: 5 students, 11-15: 8 students, 16-20: 3 students. Which class interval contains the median?
questions.explanation: Total students = 2+5+8+3 = 18. Median position = (18+1)/2 = 9.5th value. Cumulative frequencies: 2, 7, 15, 18. The 9.5th value falls in the 11-15 interval.

questions.question: The daily temperatures (°C) for a week: 22, 24, 24, 25, 26, 28, 30. What is the mode?
questions.explanation: The mode is the value that appears most frequently. 24 appears twice, more than any other value.

questions.question: Two classes took the same test. Class A: median = 65, IQR = 10. Class B: median = 65, IQR = 22. Which class had more students scoring close to the median?
questions.explanation: Same median means same middle value, but Class A has a smaller IQR (10 < 22), meaning more students scored close to the median.

questions.question: Data Set X: mean = 45, SD = 8. Data Set Y: mean = 45, SD = 3. Which statement is correct?
options: Data Set X has more consistent values
Data Set Y has more consistent values
questions.explanation: Both sets have the same mean, but Data Set Y has a smaller SD (3 < 8), meaning its values are closer to the mean — more consistent.

questions.question: A data set has values: 3, 7, 9, 12, x. If the mean is 8, what is the value of x?
Two data sets have identical means. Class X has IQR = 8, Class Y has IQR = 20. Which class has more consistent scores in the middle 50%?
questions.explanation: A smaller IQR indicates the middle 50% of scores are more tightly clustered. Class X (IQR=8) has more consistent middle scores.

questions.question: A data set has values: 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. If every value is increased by 5, what happens to the range?
questions.explanation: Range = Max - Min. Adding a constant to all values shifts both max and min by the same amount, so the range remains unchanged.
